phase: Cause-line protocol, Lite LOW. Core numeric-zero override loss exists. Boolean-default example is unsupported because actual boolean defaults are False; do not publish that example verbatim.

verification_decisions.reason: Filtering by `if v` drops valid falsy configuration values such as `False` or `0`, preventing users from overriding defaults with these values.

findings.title: Falsy configuration values (like False or 0) are dropped by `if v` filtering
findings.impact: Boolean flags (e.g. `include_source_str`, `ask_for_clarification`) and integer settings set to 0 cannot be configured to `False` or `0` because they evaluate to falsy and are filtered out, causing them to fall back unexpectedly to default values.
findings.preconditions: A user passes `include_source_str=False` or `ask_for_clarification=False` via `configurable` or environment variables when it defaults to `True`, or an integer setting is set to 0.
findings.explanation: Line 67 filters out any configuration values where `v` is falsy (`{k: v for k, v in values.items() if v}`). In Python, `False` and `0` are falsy, so they are excluded from the dictionary passed to `cls(**...)`. As a result, dataclass fields take their default values instead of the user-provided `False` or `0`.
findings.suggestion: return cls(**{k: v for k, v in values.items() if v is not None})
